To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in the BFM quantization of Yang–Mills theory the dependence on the background field of the generating functional for connected Green functions is controlled by a BRST canonical transformation, which is the natural generalization to the BFM of the BRST canonical transformation in the background independent quantization; (ii) the BRST canonical generator is given by a local functional, which is a solution of the Slavnov–Taylor identity of the model; (iii) this result is valid
in the background-field method (BFM): the background field can be gauged away, and the gauge-fixing term is independent of the background field.

the background field method in Yang-Mills theory can be consistently formulated in the presence of a non-vanishing background field, and that the dependence of the generating functional on the background gauge field can be expressed in terms of a canonical transformation w. r. t. the Batalini-Vilkovisky-BRST bracket.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Slavnov–Taylor identities of the Yang–Mills theory in the background field gauge, which is an important ingredient of nonperturbative approaches to Yang–Mills theories.
the study of the non-trivial backgrounds in the Yang-Mills theory.
a general study of the Batalin-Fradkin-Vilkovisky formalism, in particular with the Batalin-Tyutin formalism, which is the quantization procedure for gauge theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Batalin- Vilkovisky formalism provides a general and consistent framework for the BFM in Yang-Mills theory in both perturbative and non-perturbatice contexts.
the Batalin-Fradkin-Vilkovisky formalism, which has been developed in a purely perturbative context, is a powerful tool to study Yang-Mills theory in general, including non-perturbatively.

the BFM in Yang-Mills theory is not only consistent with the Slavnov- Taylor identity, but also provides a canonical transformation of the theory, which is controlled by the Slavnovic-Taylor identity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Slavnov–Taylor identity is a very strong constraint on the theory and it allows to derive the background-field quantization in the nonperturbative regime.
we show that the background field method is a canonical transformation in Yang-Mills theory, and that this is a general property that holds in perturbation theory as well as non-perturbatively.
in the BFM the background field dependence is a canonical transformation w. r. t. the BRST symmetry.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, as far as the dependence of the quantum effective action on the background is concerned, the Slavnov Taylor identity provides the same information in the perturbative and in the nonperturbative regimes, and this is true for any gauge choice, including the Landau and Coulomb gauges.
the Batalin-Fradkin-Vilkovisky formalism is not needed in the background field approach, and that the Bataln-Fradkin-Vilokovisky formalism does not offer any advantage over the standard BFM.
